title: Rollout Readiness — Weekly Ops Scratchpad
content:
Purpose / context:
This is my working scratchpad for the weekly rollout-readiness sync (internal ops cadence). Focus is to surface blockers, validate go/no-go criteria across vectors (infra, runtime, metrics, docs, comms), and track concrete assignees for preflight work. Not polished — intentionally conversational so I can jot updates during the meeting and follow up with action items.

Upcoming milestone: staged launch to Dedicated customers and Hosted API Canary on 2026-03-12. Weekly meeting cadence: Thursdays 09:30 PT. This sheet captures items for this week (meeting 2026-03-05).

Meeting attendees (planned):
- Product: Priya Rao
- Release Eng / SRE: Ethan Kim, Liam O'Connor
- Serving Runtime: Ben Zhou (recused for limited parts)
- Platform Eng: Sofia Martinez
- Solutions Eng / SEs: Amber Li
- Ops owner (me): Maya Patel

Top-level ask for this sync:
1) Confirm no critical-blocking issues remain that would violate go/no-go criteria below.
2) Validate ownership and completion windows for each checklist item.
3) Agree on canary ramp schedule and automatic rollback triggers.

High-level go/no-go criteria (must all be green OR explicitly waived):
- Infra & capacity: Dedicated GPU pools provisioned with autoscale policy validated (ENG-4123).
- End-to-end acceptance tests: nightly regression suite passing 3 consecutive runs on canary model + smoke on mainline.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile within target under expected canary load (<= 210ms).
- Cost profile: Quantization/instance mix within expected cost window (est. per-token $0.0008).
- Observability: Dashboards for token-level cost/latency, tracing hooks, and alerting thresholds wired to PagerDuty.
- Rollout automation: automatic fallback configured (roll forward/back) and playbook reviewed.
- Customer comms: SE playbook and incident contact list updated.

Current status summary (quick bullets):
- Infra: pools created; autoscaler test largely green but we saw a flakey scale-down timing issue in staging (Ethan investigating).
- E2E tests: two nightly runs passed; third run failed on a nondeterministic concurrency edge (race in request batching) — linked MR to fix batching window.
- Latency: baseline numbers look good in canary but there is a spike pattern correlated to KV cache misses at ~30s mark. Ben and Liam dug into cache warming; next plan: add prefix caching warm-up on canary start.
- Observability: dashboards built; alert thresholds drafted but not yet committed to PagerDuty escalation (SRE oncall policy needs approval).
- Comms: SE playbook draft ready; customer-facing email template awaiting legal review.

Key blockers / risks (ranked):
1) Batching race leading to sporadic tail latency — severity: high; owner: Ben; target fix MR opens today (ENG-4189). Impact: might push go to next week if not mitigated with a config-level workaround.
2) Autoscaler scale-down flake causing transient capacity shortfall during quick burst tests — severity: medium; owner: Ethan. Mitigation: temporary min-replicas bump to avoid aggressive scale-down for canary.
3) PagerDuty escalation mapping incomplete — severity: medium-low; owner: Liam. Impact acceptable if manual escalation instructions in playbook are explicit.
4) Legal review delay on the customer email template — severity: low; owner: Priya; requested turn-around 48h.

Preflight checklist (rows are 'item — owner — status — notes'):
- Canary config checklist — Priya Rao — in_progress — needs final model pin and token limits set.
- Autoscaler policy test — Ethan Kim — in_progress — repro'd scale-down flake; suggested interim min_replicas=2.
- Batching race MR (#272) review + staging deploy — Ben Zhou — in_review — must land and pass nightly run.
- KV cache warmup job added to canary boot — Liam O'Connor — todo — script ready; scheduling step gated on MR.
- E2E regression 3x runs — Maya Patel — in_progress — 2/3 done; 3rd failing due to batching race.
- Metrics & dashboards committed to infra repo — Sofia Martinez — done — dashboards live in Grafana staging.
- PagerDuty mapping committed — Liam O'Connor — todo — waiting for org-wide oncall policy confirmation.
- SE playbook final review — Amber Li & Priya Rao — in_review — legal review pending.
- Rollback automation & playbook test (DRY run) — Ethan Kim — todo — scheduled 2026-03-08.
- Customer communications draft — Priya Rao — in_review — legal/PR feedback loop.

Concrete actions decided for this week (owner — action — due):
- Ben — land batching MR with short-term mitigation if full fix slips; push staging deploy by EOD 2026-03-05. — due 2026-03-05
- Ethan — apply min_replicas bump to canary autoscaler and run burst test; report perf numbers. — due 2026-03-06
- Liam — add cache-warmup job and test on canary boot; share logs. — due 2026-03-07
- Priya — chase legal on email template and provide final SE playbook link to SEs. — due 2026-03-06
- Maya (me) — coordinate nightly regression runs and ensure 3 consecutive green runs recorded; escalate if fail. — due 2026-03-09
- Sofia — lock Grafana dashboards and create short runbook link for oncall in the playbook. — due 2026-03-06

Canary ramp plan (proposal to confirm in meeting):
- Day 0 (canary start): route 1% of Hosted traffic + 1 Dedicated customer class A (low QPS). Warmup jobs run.
- Day 1: ramp to 5% traffic; run synthetic spike test at 2h mark.
- Day 2: if metrics stable, 20% traffic and add a 2nd Dedicated customer class.
- Day 3: if stable, open to general Dedicated capacity and consider 50% traffic.
- Abort conditions: sustained 95th pctl > target for more than 30m, error rate > 0.5% for 10m, or any P0 customer-impacting bug. Automatic rollback triggers defined in MR #272.

Rollback and postmortem expectations:
- Rollback authority: SRE lead oncall + Release Eng (Ethan) can trigger automated rollback. SEs to standby for customer impact calls.
- Post-rollback: immediate incident channel, preserve request traces and token-level costs, collect a 24h heatmap and run repro tests. Postmortem to be authored within 72h and include action items and owner assignments.

Communication plan:
- Internal: Slack channel #launch-2026-03 (ops pins), daily 09:30 PT quick sync during canary week.
- Customers: targeted email to pilot/dedicated customers from Priya once canary stable for 48h.
- Public: blog/announcements only after dedicated pool available and latency SLOs verified.

Notes / discussion points to raise in meeting:
- Are we comfortable waiving PagerDuty full mapping if playbook includes explicit manual escalation steps?
- If batching MR doesn't land in time, propose temporary concurrency cap to reduce exposure; need cost/latency trade-off numbers.
- Confirm who will be the single comms lead for immediate customer outreach post-go.

My personal follow-ups after the meeting (quick checklist):
- Send meeting notes and action list to attendees (include deadlines).
- Update ENG-4123 with this week's autoscaler test results and decision (min_replicas toggle).
- Monitor nightly run status and ping Ben/Ethan immediately on failures.
- If go deferred, draft suggested schedule for next try with clear gating items.

Last-minute scraps / ad-hoc thoughts:
- Consider adding a short-lived feature-flag to disable continuous batching when we detect high KV-miss rates — might buy time without a full code rollback.
- Keep a short list of canary customers who are ok with debugging calls — saves time when mobilizing SEs.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and push to Confluence as a cleaned "runbook-lite" if we hit green by Thu EOD.
